Vide this order I shall dispose off the 'Detailed Accident Report' (hereinafter referred to as 'DAR')
filed by the police with regard to the accident occurred on 08.06.2021 in which injured Pawan Kumar (hereinafter referred to as 'petitioner') suffered injuries.
Investigating official produced petitioner as well as Jagdish Parsad (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 1'),

Rajpal (hereinafter referred to as 'respondent no. 2'), who are driver and owner of vehicle i.e. truck bearing registration no. RJ02GC 1020 (hereinafter referred to Pawan Kumar Vs. Jagdish Parsad & Ors.

Copy of DAR was supplied to all the parties.

2. In brief, the facts of the case are that during the investigation, the investigating officer recorded the statement of injured / petitioner Pawan Kumar under Section 161 CrPC, which is reproduced as under: -
"On 07/06/2021 at around 10 pm, I was riding my motorcycle No. DL-8SCK-1003 and was coming from Bawana towards Pooth Khurd.

As soon as I started turning my motorcycle back in front of Valmiki Hospital, the driver of a truck No.
RJ-02-GC-1020 was coming towards Pooth Khurd village driving his truck at a very high speed and in zigzag manner and hit my motorcycle due to which my motorcycle fell on the road and the tyre of the truck went over my right leg due to which my leg got hurt badly.
The truck driver ran away from there very fast.
The truck driver has caused me injury by driving his truck carelessly.
Legal action should be taken against him."

3. It is further matter of record that a criminal case FIR No. 348/22 under Section 279/338 IPC was registered in PS Bawana and Police Investigation Report under Section 173 Cr.PC under the above Pawan Kumar vs Jagdish Parsad on 4 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/59895257/
3 FIR was filed against driver of the vehicle in question for causing the above said accident.
4.

Respondents no. 1 & 2 (driver & owner of the offending vehicle) in their joint written statement stated that respondent no. 1 has not caused the accident and present case is based on false and fabricated story.

It is further stated that respondent no. 1 was having valid driving licence and vehicle of respondent no. 2 was duly insured with respondent no. 3 / Ins. Co. as on the date of accident and hence they are not liable to pay any compensation.
On merit, they denied all the other facts of accident and stated that it is a false case against them.

My issue-wise findings are as under:-
 ISSUE No.1:
Whether injured / petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 08.06.2021 at 10.00 pm at Opp. MV Hospital, Pooth Khurd, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing registration no. RJ-02GC 1020 by respondent no. 1 (Jagdish Prasad)?

OPP. Onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner and to prove that she suffered injuries in this accident on account of rash and negligence on the part of respondent no. 1, petitioner examined himself as PW1 and tendered his affidavit Ex.PW1/A in evidence.

Petitioner as PW1 has deposed that on 07.06.2021, he was going from Bawana to Pooth Khurd, Delhi by his motorcycle and at about 10 pm when he reached near Valmiki Hospital, all of a sudden, vehicle i.e. truck bearing registration no. RJ02GC 1020, driven by its driver in a rash, negligent, zigzag manner came and hit his motorcycle due to which he along with his motorcycle fell down on road and vehicle in question ran over his right leg and he suffered grievous injuries.

PW1 has not at all been cross examined by the respondents no. 1 and 2 particularly by the respondent no. 1 to prove that he was not rash and negligent or that he has been falsely implicated in the present case or that accident had occurred due to negligence on the part of petitioner itself.
In his cross examination by Ins. Co., no suggestion put to the PW1 with regard to manner in which the accident had occurred and he denied that accident had occurred due to his own negligence.

Further, respondent no. 1, being driver of offending vehicle was himself material witness to throw light by testifying as to how and under what circumstances and manner,
the accident has taken place but he opted not to enter into the witness box and did not lead any evidence.
Further, there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity Pawan Kumar Vs. Jagdish Parsad & Ors.

Further, criminal case record filing along with the DAR collectively Ex. PW1/1 shows that respondent no.1 was charge sheeted by the police for offences punishable under Section 279/338 IPC.
Apart from deposition of PW1, the fact that petitioner suffered injuries in the accident is also supported by his medical documents i.e. MLC etc. filed along with DAR.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.

Further, relying upon the judgment of Mahila Dhanvanti and Ors Vs.
Phulwant Mahendra Singh, Miscellaneous Appeal no.239/1992 decided by Hon'ble Madhya Pradesh High Court on 29.07.1993 in which it is held as under: -

This hardship is to be avoided by applying the principle of res ipsa loquitur.

The general purport of the words res ipsa loquitur is that the accident speaks for itself or tells its own story".
10.
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".

Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and petitioner suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.

Issue no. 1 is accordingly decided in favour of petitioner and against the respondents holding that injured / petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident occurred on 08.06.2021 at 10.00 pm at Opp. MV Hospital, Pooth Khurd, Delhi due to rash and negligent driving of vehicle bearing registration Pawan Kumar Vs.

As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured,
petitioner is the natural eye-witness of accident and is well within his rights to claim compensation from the respondents.

12.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in "Sarla Verma v. Delhi Transport Corporation" (2009),
held as under: -
"Just compensation" is adequate compensation which is fair and equitable, on the facts and circumstances of the case, to make good the loss suffered as a result of the wrong, as far as money can do so, by applying the well settled principles relating to award of compensation.

18.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Further, there is nothing on record to show that the petitioner had any enmity Pawan Kumar Vs. Jagdish Parsad & Ors.
Respondent no. 1 has not placed on record any document to disprove the factum of rash and negligent driving by him.
Thus, Claims Tribunal while dealing with the law of torts in motor accident cases applies the principle of "res ipsa loquitur".
Considering all this, it stands proved that accident in question occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending vehicle by the respondent no. 1 and petitioner suffered grievous injuries in the said accident.
As far as the issue with respect to right to claim compensation is concerned, being injured,
petitioner is the natural eye-witness of accident and is well within his rights to claim compensation from the respondents.
Section 168 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, mandate the Tribunal to hold an inquiry into claims under section 166 and to determine the amount of compensation which appears to be just and reasonable.
Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the fact that petitioner has suffered 80% permanent disability in relation to right lower limb i.e. amputation and following the principles of justice, equity and good conscience and to adopt more realistic, Pawan Kumar Vs. Jagdish Parsad & Ors.
pragmatic and liberal approach, the tribunal is of the view that such kind of amputation would definitely hamper day to day activity and work for gain throughout his entire life.
Hence, functional disability / percentage of loss of earning capacity in relation to disability is taken as 40% qua whole body.
15. As far as loss of income on account of loss of future earning due to disability is concerned,
petitioner as PW1 deposed that he was 30 years in age and was working in Civil Defense and earning Rs. 22,000/- per month and due to permanent disability he is unable to work for rest of his life.

a multiplier of 17, as per the as per the judgment passed by Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in the case of Sarla Verma vs Delhi Transport Corporation, 2009 ACJ 1298, is taken for calculating his loss to future earnings.
Accordingly, this amount of Rs.23,96,298.24p is allowed to the petitioner, as loss of future earnings, due to permanent disability.
No tax is deducted since the said income of petitioner is not taxable.
opennyai_summary.arguments:
Though no evidence has placed on record, however considering the nature of injuries as the petitioner has suffered permanent disability that too amputation, it is presumed that petitioner would have availed the services of an attendant.
Accordingly, a lump sum amount of Rs.60,000/- is awarded to the petitioner towards attendant charges.
Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi and others, of Hon'ble Supreme Court, petitioner is also entitled to get 40% of enhancement of salary, as he was below 40 years in age at the time of accident.
